requirement: Make an LLM call resilient with a LangChain-like with_fallbacks chain that switches models only on expected errors and reports the original failure when every option fails.
skeleton: A RateLimitError, a RunnableLambda with invoke and with_fallbacks, and a RunnableWithFallbacks that validates its fallbacks, tries runnables in order on selected exceptions, records attempts and re-raises the first error.
caption: LangChain-style runnables with fallbacks written in the standard library with collections.abc and typing and no third-party imports. RateLimitError is a plain Exception. RunnableLambda wraps a function and a name, invoke calls it, and with_fallbacks takes a list of runnables and exceptions_to_handle defaulting to Exception only, so KeyboardInterrupt is never swallowed. RunnableWithFallbacks raises ValueError without fallbacks. invoke resets attempts, then tries each runnable in order, recording its name and returning the first result; only exceptions in exceptions_to_handle move on to the next runnable while others propagate at once, and when every runnable fails it re-raises the first handled error, an assertion guarding that one exists. names lists the order. The fixture asserts primary success, ordered fallbacks, immediate propagation of unhandled errors, the first error when all fail, per-call attempts, KeyboardInterrupt propagation and the ValueError.

constraints: Creating a chain without fallbacks raises ValueError
Only exceptions_to_handle trigger the next runnable; others propagate
The default handles Exception, never KeyboardInterrupt
When all runnables fail the first handled error is re-raised
attempts reflects only the latest invoke

rationale.teaches: Catch only the configured exception types, try runnables in order, and surface the primary error when every fallback also fails.
rationale.why: Catching everything hides programming bugs behind backup models, and re-raising the last error blames the backup instead of the real cause.

ops.docstring: LangChain-style runnables with ordered fallbacks on selected exceptions.

ops.source:
class RateLimitError(Exception):
    """Raised by a model that is temporarily over quota."""

candidates.why_wrong: When every runnable fails the last fallback's error is raised instead of the primary's.
KeyboardInterrupt is caught by default and the chain keeps calling fallbacks.
attempts keeps names from earlier calls and grows across invocations.
Programming errors like KeyError are swallowed and routed to the fallback model.
A chain without fallbacks is accepted and silently behaves like the bare primary.
